name: Hungerburgbahn Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: The Hungerburg Funicular in Innsbruck: Zaha Hadid's architectural masterpiece linking the historic city centre to the Hungerburg plateau in eight minutes.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Hungerburgbahn (Hungerburg Funicular) is an avant-garde hybrid funicular railway in Tyrol's provincial capital Innsbruck, linking the city centre at the Congress terminal with the panoramic district of Hungerburg at an elevation of 860 metres. Designed by the internationally acclaimed architect Zaha Hadid and inaugurated in December 2007, the railway stands as a globally celebrated milestone of contemporary alpine architecture. The four futuristic stations (Congress, Löwenhaus, Alpenzoo, and Hungerburg) feature sweeping, snow-white glass canopy shells inspired by natural glacial ice formations.

Route & Requirements

Covering a track length of 1,838 metres, the funicular ascends a vertical height of 288 metres in just eight minutes. The ride is both an engineering and architectural triumph: departing underground beneath the imperial Hofgarten, the train crosses the turquoise River Inn across an elegant S-shaped cable-stayed bridge supported by an inclined steel pylon, before ascending the steep flanks of the Nordkette mountains via elevated viaducts. An ingenious automatic levelling system tilts the passenger pods during steep gradients of up to 46 percent, ensuring passengers remain comfortably level throughout the ride. An intermediate stop serves the Alpenzoo—home to Europe's highest themed wildlife park. At the mountain terminal on the Hungerburg plateau, visitors enjoy sweeping panoramic vistas over Innsbruck and the Tux Alps, with direct onward connections to the Nordkettenbahnen cable cars ascending to the Hafelekar (2,256 m) at the Top of Innsbruck.

Visit & Arrival

The Hungerburgbahn operates daily at 15-minute intervals from 07:15 to 19:15 (from 08:00 on weekends and public holidays). Return ticket prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €12.50, youth/seniors approx. €10.00, children (ages 6 to 15) approx. €7.00, children under 6 free. Unlimited rides are included in the comprehensive Innsbruck Card. Base station address: Rennweg 3, adjacent to the historic Old Town. Arriving by car: park at the underground City or Congress garage (discounted parking available when purchasing funicular tickets). By public transit: just a 5-minute stroll from the Golden Roof; bus and tram stop Congress/Hofburg served by lines 1, 3, A, R, and 504.

Tips

All stations and carriages are step-free and fully accessible for wheelchairs and strollers via modern elevators. Combine your ascent with the Alpenzoo combo ticket for discounted zoo entry. An evening ride at dusk is particularly magical, as Zaha Hadid's luminous glass canopies glow warmly against the glittering city lights below.
preis: Round-trip ticket adults approx. €12.50, children approx. €7.00 (free with Innsbruck Card)
